news.headline: RBI MPC Hikes Repo Rate 25 bps to 5.50% — First Hike Since Feb 2023
news.what_happened: The RBI raised repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50%, shifting stance to calibrated tightening. Governor Sanjay Malhotra cited rising crude and rupee risks. FY27 inflation forecast raised to 5.2%, GDP outlook lifted to 7.1%.
news.why_it_matters: First hike since Feb 2023 shocks rate-sensitive sectors. Banks face bond portfolio mark-downs and NIM compression. NBFCs face higher cost of funds. Home loan rates rise, hurting real estate. Biggest single domestic macro shock of the week.

news.headline: Brent Crude Crosses $102/bbl — WTI at $89.63 (+1.53%)
news.what_happened: Global crude surged on continued OPEC+ supply discipline and geopolitical risk. Brent crossed $100 to hit $102, up 1.80%. WTI rose 1.53% to $89.63.
news.why_it_matters: Crude above $100 is a double blow for India — widens current account deficit and fuels inflation (already prompting RBI hike). Bearish for airlines, paints, tyres, logistics. Strongly bullish for upstream oil ONGC and OIL India.

news.headline: FII Net Sold Rs 6,121 Cr on Oct 7 — MTD Selling at Rs 23,266 Cr
news.what_happened: FIIs sold Rs 18,699 Cr and bought only Rs 12,578 Cr in cash markets on Oct 7. Net selling: Rs 6,121.37 Cr. DIIs bought Rs 4,597 Cr — absorbing only 75% of FII outflows. MTD FII selling: Rs 23,266 Cr.
news.why_it_matters: Persistent FII selling combined with US 10Y at 5.277% signals continued capital outflow headwind. Large caps with high FII ownership face sustained selling pressure.

news.headline: China Markets Reopen After Golden Week — Weak Holiday Consumer Spending
news.what_happened: Mainland Chinese markets reopen Thursday after a 7-day National Day holiday. Bloomberg reports consumer spending was weak. Offshore China stocks fell 1.7% during the closure, leaving CSI 300 vulnerable to selling.
news.why_it_matters: China is the world's largest buyer of base metals. Weak reopening + demand concerns are bearish for Indian metal exporters — steel, aluminium, copper all face headwinds.

news.headline: USD/INR at 96.75 (+0.40%) — Rupee Near Year-High Weakness
news.what_happened: Rupee weakened to 96.75/USD driven by FII outflows and elevated crude import costs. Year-high is 96.96.
news.why_it_matters: Tailwind for IT and pharma exporters — USD revenues convert to more INR. TCS reports today; rupee at 96.75 provides margin boost. Headwind for airlines (dollar fuel costs).

news.headline: TCS Q2 FY27 Results Today + GST Council 57th Meeting
news.what_happened: TCS reports Q2 FY27 earnings today, kicking off earnings season. GST Council meets for potential rate rationalization in pharma, FMCG, telecom.
news.why_it_matters: TCS beat could lift IT sector. Rupee at 96.75 boosts margin. GST decisions will be event-specific for pharma, FMCG, telecom stocks and may cause sharp intraday moves.

picks.catalyst: Brent crude at $102/bbl (+1.80%), WTI $89.63 (+1.53%) — multi-month high on OPEC+ supply discipline
picks.logic: ONGC's revenue is directly pegged to crude oil realization. Brent crossing $102 is a strong earnings catalyst — every $5/bbl rise adds ~Rs 3,500-4,000 Cr to annual net profit. Stock fell 1.04% yesterday due to broad RBI-driven sell-off, creating a disconnect from the fundamental crude tailwind. Catch-up opportunity as oil prices outrun the stock's reaction.

picks.catalyst: Gold at $4,161.80/oz (+0.51%) + USD/INR at 96.75 (+0.40%) — dual tailwind from gold price and rupee weakness
picks.logic: Muthoot Finance is India's largest gold loan NBFC with ~99% gold-backed loan book. Higher gold prices elevate collateral values, lower LTV risk, enable loan book expansion. Weak INR at 96.75 amplifies the INR value of gold. Stock fell 1.18% yesterday in broad RBI-driven sell-off — oversold versus fundamentals given the gold price surge.
